name: The thieving senses (kaḷḷap pulaṉ)
description: The five senses as thieves and a forest to be cut down and burnt before the 'house' of release can be seen (Kaṭuveḷi 13–14); cut off by the guru (Aḻukaṇṇi 34); burnt by the seeker (Pattirakiriyār 1); TM 1823 calls them the thieving senses that become the temple's lamps once tamed.

name: The three desires (ēṭaṇai)
description: Kaṭuveḷi: 'the three desires are evil' (5); in the Siddha list of ninety-six they are the desires for wife, children and wealth (list recalled at low confidence).

name: The eight passions (irākam)
description: Among the ninety-six principles: desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, envy, haughtiness and egoism (list recalled at low confidence).

name: The three impurities (āṇavam, kaṉmam, māyai)
description: Counted among the ninety-six principles (malam 3); Paṭṭiṉattār speaks of fleeing 'the woman called māyā-mala' to the mother, grace (Tiruvēkampamālai 10).

name: The two deeds (iruviṉai)
description: Good and bad deeds both bind: the Lord drives us 'by the rope of the two deeds' (Tiruttillai 11); one's own deed burns oneself; the knower seeks neither (Tiruvaḷḷuvar ñāṉam 13).

name: Imbalance of the three humours
description: Excess or deficiency of vaḷi, aḻal and aiyam causes disease (Kuṟaḷ 941); the tradition counts 4,448 diseases arising from it. Remedied by regimen, medicine and kaṟpam.

name: Desire for women (peṇṇācai)
description: In the renouncer-poets' own terms, desire for women is the snare that binds to birth; the seeker longs to think of woman as mother (Pattirakiriyār 8, 9–11) and Paṭṭiṉattār laments the women who bewitch. Recorded faithfully as the texts' view.

name: Intoxicants (ganja, opium, toddy)
description: Kaṭuveḷi: do not smoke ganja or drink toddy (29); Pattirakiriyār longs not to wither with ganja, opium and toddy but to drink the fivefold nectar (35).

name: False garb (kaḷḷa vēṭam)
description: The hypocrite's ascetic costume: 'do not put on a false garb' (Kaṭuveḷi 33); 'for those who conquered death, why costumes?' (Kuṭampai 26); Pattirakiriyār longs to leave the vain garb for Śiva's (28).

name: Outward ritual without inner knowledge
description: Stone images, temple rounds, holy baths, pilgrimage and recitation taken as ends: the Siddhars' main target (Sivavākkiyar; Kaṭuveḷi 15; Pattirakiriyār 16).

name: Caste pride (cāti)
description: Holding birth-group as real difference; denied by the Siddhars (Sivavākkiyar; Kaṭuveḷi 32).

name: The restless mind as demon (akappēy)
description: The mind that runs like a demon or whirls like a fish in a net, to be stilled (Akappēy's refrain; Pattirakiriyār 26); stilling it is the hardest skill (Tāyumāṉavar).

name: Powers as obstacles
description: Tāyumāṉavar: every power, from taming beasts to transmuting metals and entering other bodies, is easier than stilling the mind — the powers are not the goal; Kuṭampai asks what need the knower has of kaṟpam and yoga.
